rootCause: The skill's documented normal path for TXT files was ambiguous about actually invoking the bundled pipeline, while the bundled entry point imported optional DOCX/PDF fallback libraries at startup. In a clean environment this made the authoritative normalizer and Stage3 checker unavailable for TXT work, so the agent manually reproduced their output and asserted approval; that bypassed executable verification and allowed the evaluator-visible heading-policy mismatch to coexist with a report claiming success.
reasoning: Evidence 0 is a clean run (runStatus=ok), so it supports diagnosis. The run protected the input, preserved the source character stream, split enumerated items, and created the required artifacts, but failed both the external heading-policy criterion and the approval-outcome criterion. The workdir report says Stage3-B passed even though no process evidence shows the bundled checker ran, and the current bundled CLI could not even display --help in this clean workspace because top-level imports raised ModuleNotFoundError for docx. This explains why the agent hand-authored artifacts instead of using the parameterized pipeline. The fix routes TXT work explicitly through the bundled script, requires model document classification to be passed via --law-decision rather than merely narrated, and makes optional fallback imports lazy so routine TXT conversion and --help work without unrelated packages. Generality test: another plausible TXT statute containing parts, sections, article labels, or multiple enumerated items benefits from the same deterministic normalizer/checker path; a clean offline environment lacking PDF/DOCX fallback dependencies also benefits. Rewrite-in-place test: the existing TXT rule, Stage2 classifier rule, and command examples were tightened in place rather than duplicated in a new tutorial. Coherent-scope test: only the routing documentation and two dependency imports changed; the existing formatter/checker remains the source of formatting policy and no capability was removed. No-trade-off test: PER_TASK_SUMMARY.md contains no PASSING tasks, so there is no passing-score regression risk; the observed marginal task's already-passing input protection, source accounting, item layout, and artifact behavior are preserved by the existing script and were revalidated on its materialized fixture. Verification: `python scripts/law_to_markdown.py --help` succeeds without optional packages; all three Python files compile; and the fixture run with `--law-decision law --artifact-level minimal` produces only the two minimal artifacts, reports approval/deliverability, preserves the source stream, and passes the bundled Stage3 checks. The exact external hierarchy expectation is not exposed beyond the criterion label, so no heading levels were guessed or changed; interpretation of any external contract that differs from the skill remains an agent duty.

changes.section: 处理规则 / 常用命令
changes.description: Tighten the existing TXT workflow and examples so agents invoke the bundled verified pipeline, pass their law/non-law decision explicitly, and only claim approval from generated artifacts.
changes.generality: Any other TXT statute conversion, such as a document containing 编、节、条标 or several 项/目, benefits from deterministic formatting and approval checks instead of manual reproduction.

changes.description: Load python-docx and pdfplumber only inside their explicitly selected fallback converters so TXT conversion and CLI discovery remain runnable in clean environments.
changes.generality: Any offline or clean-environment TXT task without DOCX/PDF fallback packages benefits, while DOCX/PDF fallback tasks retain the same behavior with a clearer missing-dependency error.

opportunities.summary: The TXT rule and examples did not make bundled-script execution or the concrete classifier argument mandatory, enabling a manually narrated Stage3 approval.
opportunities.residualDuty: The agent must still classify the document using professional judgment and select law, non-law, or auto when classification is genuinely uncertain.

opportunities.summary: The existing CLI already accepts arbitrary input/output paths and --law-decision, but the examples omitted the decision parameter and did not expose the reliable routine invocation.
opportunities.residualDuty: The agent must honor task-scoped output paths and artifact-level requirements when constructing arguments.

opportunities.summary: Heading assignment, article/body splitting, whitespace cleanup, item splitting, report generation, and artifact policy are deterministic transformations already bundled in the pipeline.
opportunities.residualDuty: Manual transformation remains a fallback only when the executable genuinely cannot run; the agent must not fabricate checker results.

opportunities.summary: The bundled Stage3 checker can independently enforce source-stream preservation and the skill-declared hierarchy, but the observed report claimed its result without evidence that it ran.
opportunities.residualDuty: The agent must inspect command success and generated report/deliverable presence, and must reconcile any user-supplied contract that differs from the skill-declared hierarchy rather than assuming equivalence.

opportunities.summary: Top-level imports of optional PDF/DOCX fallback packages prevented unrelated TXT processing and even --help in a clean environment.
opportunities.residualDuty: For explicitly approved DOCX/PDF fallback, the agent must ensure the corresponding optional dependency is available; mineru-ocr installation and network restrictions remain context-dependent.

opportunities.summary: Document classification, conflict resolution between task contracts and skill policy, and final communication cannot be replaced solely by the deterministic formatter.
opportunities.residualDuty: The agent remains responsible for classification, respecting task-scoped restrictions, interpreting externally required hierarchy when explicitly supplied, and reporting only verified outcomes.

inputs: local .txt input path supplied by the task
caller classification: law, non-law, or auto
optional output directory and artifact level
outputs: review report under the selected output directory
final deliverable only when the pipeline approves it
preconditions: Python can execute the bundled script
the input is a local .txt file for the dependency-free path

constraints.description: TXT is converted through Stage2 formatting and default Stage3 verification, preserving the non-whitespace character stream.
The observed task forbids modifying the input, networking, or installing packages and requests minimal artifacts in a specified directory.
Optional python-docx and pdfplumber packages are absent in the optimization environment.

residualDuties: classify the document and pass the decision
inspect generated results and do not claim approval after a failed command
resolve explicit external hierarchy requirements not established by the skill source
verification: run `python scripts/law_to_markdown.py --help` without optional fallback packages
run the materialized TXT fixture with law decision and minimal artifacts
confirm Stage3 A/B PASS, exactly two minimal output files, report approval, and unchanged input
